title: Compass rose round
subtitle: An eight-section circular motif with alternating long and short points in two colours
excerpt: Eight sections alternate between four long treble-spike cardinal points and four shorter htr intercardinal points, giving the compass rose its distinctive asymmetric star outline. Worked in two colours — one per point type — the motif reads clearly from across a room.
sourceNotes: Compass rose and directional motifs appear in Victorian needlework collections from the 1880s. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889).
heroPrompt: A compass rose crochet motif in navy and cream DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Four long cardinal points and four shorter intercardinal points alternating around the circle, 13 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished compass rose measures 13 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Compass rose round
chartDefinition.caption: Eight sections alternating tall (treble spike) and short (htr spike). Two colours, one per spike type.

glossaryTerms.definition: In a compass rose motif, one of the four longer points (N, S, E, W) worked in trebles, contrasted with the shorter intercardinal points (NE, SE, SW, NW) worked in half trebles.

content.text: The compass rose alternates four tall

in colour A with four shorter intercardinal points in colour B. The cardinal points use stitch stepping up to a chain-2 tip; the intercardinal points reach only to htr height. This difference in length gives the compass rose its distinctive uneven star outline.

The finished motif requires blocking with all 8 points pinned open. Navy and cream is the classic colourway; any high-contrast pair works. Avoid similar tones — the motif reads by colour contrast as much as by stitch height.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 7 g colour A and 5 g colour B in DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Blocking mat and 8 pins.

content.text: Round 1: magic ring, 16 dc into ring, sl st join. (Sets 16 base positions, 2 per point section.)

Round 2: work alternate sections in colours A and B. On colour-A sections (every other pair of sts): 1 dc, 1 htr, 2 tr, 1 htr, 1 dc (long cardinal point). On colour-B sections: 1 dc, 1 htr, 1 dc (short intercardinal point). Sl st between sections.
Round 3: extend each point. Cardinal (A): 2 dc up one side, 3 tr, ch 2 tip, 3 tr, 2 dc down. Sl st valley. Intercardinal (B): 1 dc, 2 htr, ch 1 tip, 2 htr, 1 dc. Sl st valley. Fasten off.
